title: [NEXT-1315] Opengraph image metadata unfilled segment on windows

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body:
### Verify canary release

* [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
      Platform: win32
      Arch: x64
      Version: Windows 10 Pro
    Binaries:
      Node: 18.12.1
      npm: N/A
      Yarn: N/A
      pnpm: N/A
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.4.7-canary.1
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.6
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
      typescript: 5.1.3
```

### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

App directory (appDir: true), Metadata (metadata, generateMetadata, next/head, head.js), Operating System (Windows, MacOS, Linux)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

[https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/next-issue-opengraph-image-metadata-wrong-segment-696w7t](https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/next-issue-opengraph-image-metadata-wrong-segment-696w7t)

### To Reproduce

1. Create `opengraph-image.(ts|tsx|js|jsx)` with the default handler function and `generateImageMetadata` function.
2. The image endpoint itself is working correctly and the metadata supposedly\* fills the path params (e.g. `/[slug]/opengraph-image/medium` to `/test/opengraph-image/medium`).
3. Navigate to `/test/` (which will matches with path `/[slug]/page.tsx` respectively), and inspect the HTML

* If the server is running on a non-Windows machine, the generated opengraph meta tags will be

```
<meta property="og:image:type" content="image/png">
<meta property="og:image" content="http://localhost:3000/test/opengraph-image/medium?e45377ccef76c40b">
<meta property="og:image:width" content="800">
<meta property="og:image:height" content="400">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">
<meta name="twitter:image:type" content="image/png">
<meta name="twitter:image" content="http://localhost:3000/test/opengraph-image/medium?e45377ccef76c40b">
<meta name="twitter:image:width" content="800">
<meta name="twitter:image:height" content="400">
```

* Otherwise, if the server is running on Windows:

```
<meta property="og:image:type" content="image/png">
<meta property="og:image" content="http://localhost:3000/[slug]/opengraph-image/medium?e45377ccef76c40b">
<meta property="og:image:width" content="800">
<meta property="og:image:height" content="400">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary">
<meta name="twitter:image:type" content="image/png">
<meta name="twitter:image" content="http://localhost:3000/[slug]/opengraph-image/medium?e45377ccef76c40b">
<meta name="twitter:image:width" content="800">
<meta name="twitter:image:height" content="400">
```

\* See `fillMetadataSegment` in [next-metadata-image-loader.ts](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/b32c1ea12d2ef4077c499ebc2c7ed58b47657514/packages/next/src/build/webpack/loaders/next-metadata-image-loader.ts)

> To reproduce this issue, you must run this on Windows. *or any other operating system that use back slash, if any?*

### Describe the Bug

Basically, the problem is caused by the path separator, which is `\` in Windows and `/` in non-Windows machines. The function `fillMetadataSegment` in [get-metadata-route.ts](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/b32c1ea12d2ef4077c499ebc2c7ed58b47657514/packages/next/src/lib/metadata/get-metadata-route.ts) expects the variable `segment` to be forward-slash-separated, but the case is not true on Windows machine.

I isolated the problem by directly calling the `fillMetadataSegment` function.

![](https://uploads.linear.app/099ed59a-06c6-472f-9977-4798721bda90/134389fe-9ca2-441a-a02e-347322fe79ed/d8f16d64-204d-4afb-9202-682ca7f46eb0)

> Note: For debugging purposes, I modified the `get-metadata-route.js` file to log the variables:
>
> ```
> function fillMetadataSegment(segment, params, imageSegment) {
>     const pathname = (0, _apppaths.normalizeAppPath)(segment);
>     const routeRegex = (0, _routeregex.getNamedRouteRegex)(pathname, false);
>     const route = (0, _serverutils.interpolateDynamicPath)(pathname, params, routeRegex);
>     const suffix = getMetadataRouteSuffix(segment);
>     const routeSuffix = suffix ? `-${suffix}` : "";
>     const { name, ext } = _path.default.parse(imageSegment);
>     const result = (0, _normalizepathsep.normalizePathSep)(_path.default.join(route, `${name}${routeSuffix}${ext}`));
> +    console.log(segment, params, imageSegment, result);
>     return result;
> }
> ```

### Expected Behavior

The `[slug]` parameter should be filled by the function `fillMetadataSegment` regardless if the path is forward-slashed or back-slashed. An alternative solution would be normalizing back-slashed to forward-slashed in [next-metadata-image-loader.ts](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/b32c1ea12d2ef4077c499ebc2c7ed58b47657514/packages/next/src/build/webpack/loaders/next-metadata-image-loader.ts).

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

*No response*

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

next start, on windows
